0.long_answer: The enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of unsulfated α-L-iduronosidic linkages in dermatan sulfate is α-L-iduronidase. This lysosomal hydrolase is critical for degrading glycosaminoglycans such as dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate. A deficiency in α-L-iduronidase leads to the accumulation of these substances, resulting in mucopolysaccharidosis type I (MPS I), which includes Hurler syndrome. Thus, when α-L-iduronidase is deficient, the impaired breakdown of glycosaminoglycans leads to the clinical manifestations observed in Hurler syndrome.
